title: Throwing Shade
desc:
My work titled 'Throwing Shade' is a realistic depiction of a satirical representation of the 2 greats - Salvador Dali and Pablo Picasso. I have imagined them getting together and viewing modern day art and not looking pleased. The humour lies in the fact that they were known as much for their quirky personalities as they were for their unique art styles. The additional satire lies in the title - a modern day slang term for looking disdainful.
Medium - Pencil and charcoal on paper.
Size - 60 x 40 cm.

title: “आत्म“
desc:
This self-portrait is not just an image of me—it is a reflection of every woman who carries strength with
grace. Through detailed tones, traditional jewellery,
and expressive eyes, I wanted to capture the quiet confidence that women hold
within them—whether they speak loudly or silently.
This artwork is a tribute to
womanhood: to the
ones who nurture, build, fight, lead, and still remain soft. It celebrates identity,
culture, resilience, and the beauty of being unapologetically yourself. A reminder that behind every
smile is a story, and within every woman is power.

title: More hands
desc:
More Hands is a self-portrait that explores my relationship with creativity, ambition, and the limitations of the human body. The painting emerged from a recurring feeling that a single pair of hands is not enough to realize all the ideas, projects, and aspirations that occupy my mind. Through the image of my own figure transformed with additional limbs, I examine the desire to create beyond what is physically possible.
In the painting, I depict myself engaged in drawing, a fundamental act of observation and creation. The extra hands extending from my body symbolize the many roles I occupy simultaneously as an artist, thinker, maker, and observer. They represent my wish to work on multiple ideas at once and to keep pace with an imagination that often moves faster than my ability to execute it. At the same time, these additional limbs suggest the pressure that accompanies creative ambition and the constant pursuit of improvement.
The work draws inspiration from Kamaji in Howl's Moving Castle, whose many arms allow him to perform several tasks simultaneously. I was fascinated by this image because it mirrors my own experience as an artist. I often feel the need for more hands to paint, draw, build, experiment, and develop new ideas all at once. Kamaji became a visual metaphor for the endless demands of creative practice and the desire to extend the limits of what a single body can accomplish.
Rather than presenting a conventional likeness, this self-portrait becomes a symbolic representation of my creative state of mind. Through expressive brushwork and exaggerated anatomy, More Hands reflects on the tension between artistic ambition and human limitation. It is a meditation on the desire to create more while accepting that every work of art is ultimately shaped by the same pair of hands.

title: Newly Married Girl (Watercolour) [2.5 × 3 feet]
desc: This painting depicts a newly married woman cooking for the first time in her new household. Standing in an unfamiliar kitchen, she faces heat and smoke while adapting to a role she may not have chosen. The work reflects both personal emotional adjustment and the societal expectation that marriage immediately confines women to domestic responsibility. Through this work, I express the silent emotional transition women undergo after marriage.

title: Inner Reflection
desc: This painting uses bright, thick colors and bold strokes to show deep thinking and inner feelings. While there is a storm of colorful thoughts inside the mind, the eyes stay calm and focused.

title: A Nicolas Cage Portrait
desc: Nicolas Cage rendered in watercolor. Exploring vibrant layers, raw emotion, and dramatic contrast on paper.

title: Rustic man
desc:

Size : 18/24 inches
India every state have have various aspect of human life .I painted Rajasthani Rustic man .
I painted this portrait in soft pastel .

title: Serenity
desc: A quiet Study of inner focus .The figure isn't just reading a book, but withdrawing into thought .The soft light isolates him from the world, suggesting that true understanding happens in solitude, where attention becomes  almost sacred .And in this day and age of technology and fast paced environments the art of reading has almost become lost.

title: The Artist Within
desc:
Medium - oil on paper

Size-14in/20in

This painting captures a quiet moment of creativity and concentration. The subject holding a brush represents the personal connection between an artist and their work. I was inspired by the natural expression and the beauty of an ordinary creative moment. Loose, visible brushstrokes, layered colours, and strong light and shadow were used to give the portrait a lively and expressive feel. The combination of teal, dark tones, and warm skin tones creates contrast while keeping the mood calm and intimate. The work celebrates creativity, individuality, and the simple joy of making art.

title: Love portrait (दादा जी)
desc: यह मेरे दादाजी की लाइव ऑयल पेंटिंग है, जिसे मैंने रात्रि के समय कृत्रिम प्रकाश में प्रत्यक्ष अवलोकन के आधार पर बनाया है। मेरे दादाजी एक किसान हैं और बचपन से मैंने उनके कठिन परिश्रम, संघर्ष और परिवार के प्रति प्रेम को देखा है। इस चित्र में Chiaroscuro Oil Painting Technique के माध्यम से प्रकाश और गहरी छाया द्वारा उनके व्यक्तित्व को व्यक्त करने का प्रयास किया है। चेहरे पर पड़ता प्रकाश उनके परिवार के प्रति प्रेम और स्नेह का प्रतीक है, जबकि गहरी छाया उनके जीवनभर के संघर्ष और परिश्रम को दर्शाती है।  पोर्ट्रेट  करने की प्रेरणा मुझे सर प्रमोद कुर्लेकर और सर रिचर्ड स्मिथ के कलाकृतियों से मिली।

title: Aaru - Portrait of My Daughter
desc: A portrait of my daughter, painted with a focus on looseness and immediacy. Rather than detailing everything, I wanted to let the brushwork, broken colour, and atmosphere carry the feeling of the moment.

title: Grace
desc: The work ‘Grace’ is a Portrait Composition in Acrylic on Canvas and size 30”x 24” inches. It conveys the artistic freedom of medium and texture while maintaining the disciplined academic principles according to the portrait composition. The work is loose and bold in its approach and displays natural artistic expression.

title: The humble neighbour
desc: The Humble Neighbour is a tribute to the people who have inspired and shaped me from an early age. The painting portrays an intellectual neighbour of mine, quietly absorbed in a book, carrying the classic side bag once emblematic of the Bengali intellectual and leftist culture of an earlier generation. The work embodies my gratitude towards the thoughtful adults who surrounded me while growing up and profoundly influenced the person I have become. The word “neighbour” signifies their enduring presence close to me. Ultimately, the painting is a visual homage to the intellect and wisdom the world has offered me.

title: Manshi
desc: While creating this painting, I have tried to capture the mood, emotions, and inner state of the person. Light and shadow play an important role in this artwork. Through the use of light, I have tried to create the atmosphere, visual drama, and depth within the painting. I have explored the expression of the person through the interplay of light, colours, and emotions. Rather than simply portraying the figure, I wanted to experience and express the joy of painting through light, emotions, and colour.

title: Noor
desc:
This painting presents a quiet and introspective portrait of a young woman seated in a simple interior. Her folded hands and distant gaze create a feeling of contemplation, silence, and emotional depth. The composition focuses strongly on her individual presence and psychological expression.

The deep red blouse becomes the central visual focus, contrasting with the soft white lower garment and the muted, earthy background. The patterned shawl adds texture and subtle decorative detail, while the large earthen pot in the foreground contributes to a sense of domestic space and everyday life.

The painting uses soft, expressive brushwork and a restrained colour palette, creating an atmosphere that feels both realistic and poetic. The unfinished and textured background enhances the sense of mood rather than describing a specific location. Overall, the work communicates identity, inner emotion, simplicity, and the quiet dignity of an ordinary individual.

title: Face of Rajsthan
desc: This is a realistic portrait of a traditional Rajasthani man, featuring a vibrant red turban, white moustache, and expressive facial details. The warm colors and fine brushwork beautifully capture his character and personality.

title: Crimson
desc: This portrait is a study of my friend, where I have tried to capture not only his physical features but also his personality and natural charm. I focused on his distinctive features, expression, and relaxed pose to reflect his individuality and confidence. The deep red background adds contrast and emotional intensity to the figure. Through this work, my aim was to create a personal and honest representation of him rather than simply reproducing his appearance. I wanted the painting to convey the way I see and experience his character, making the portrait more intimate, expressive, and personal.

title: The Artist and His Art
desc: This artwork depicts the portrait of Veteran Artist G Subramanian Sir and his artworks. Artist G Subramanian Sir's artwork often depicts Gods with hooded eyes and bright red lips. Done in oil medium on canvas and as live painting, in this artwork I wanted to capture not only the Artist but also the essence of his creation.

title: Untitle
desc: There’s something I really like about drawing quiet, unposed moments. This piece was mainly about observing the gesture, the light, and the feeling of stillness in the pose. I tried to keep it loose and natural rather than overworking every detail.

title: In Quiet Waiting
desc:
This self-portrait captures a quiet, everyday moment, painted from life using a bathroom mirror setup. The lighting comes from a mix of fixtures in the bathroom and a ceiling light in the hallway behind. A black wall-mounted telephone introduces an element of waiting, while a direct gaze connects the subject with the viewer.
 Medium: Oil on paper
 Dimensions: 15 × 18 inches
 Process: Painted from life (mirror setup)

title: Longing to Belong
desc:
A portrait study painted from life in a community studio setting. The model was sat on an elevated platform and I was painting while sitting on the ground. The subject, wearing a red kurta, is set against a cool blue background under a strong main light combined with overhead ceiling fixtures. Visible, textured brushwork builds the figure, using warm ochres, oranges, and deep indigos to capture the light across the face and clothing.
Medium: Acrylic on handmade paper
Dimensions: 12 × 16 inches
Process: Painted from life (group study setup)

title: "Sleepless" self portrait
desc: “Sleepless” is a self-portrait capturing the quiet weight of exhaustion and reflection. Through layered brushstrokes and muted tones, the work portrays a moment suspended between physical fatigue and an alert, restless mind.

title: Piyush
desc: ​In this scene, I have depicted my friend Piyush using a mobile phone. I liked this scene because strong side-lighting coming from a window creates dynamic highlights on the subject's arm, face, and leg while casting deep, dramatic shadows across the room. A warm, earthy color scheme dominated by soft ochre, warm browns, and muted blues enhances the cozy, grounded atmosphere. Additionally, soft blending on the background wall provides visual depth, while defined edge control and realistic anatomical modeling give the figure a tangible, three-dimensional presence. Ultimately, the piece evokes themes of contemplation, relaxation, and everyday contemporary life.In this painting, I used oil colors on an oil paper sheet, completing it live across 3 to 4 sitting sessions. I worked layer by layer and used a limited palette.

title: Frames of a Journey - Many faces one story
desc:
A Portrait in Dry semi Hard Pastels
Size : 16 by 16 inches
This is a portrait of senior kannada actor k.Suchendra Prasad created live . Created with collage where I pasted his photographs from film journey arround my creativity, drawn film reel, and clapperboard become fragments of a larger story—celebrating a life dedicated to Kannada cinema.
Thank you for this opportunity to submit my artwork.

title: Varun
desc: This is a live portraiture done with oil pastels for which I have used the melting method to give the portrait a more dynamic feel. I have used grey tones for the shadows and the base and added some vibrant tones later to make the portrait pop. I have maintained the rawness of the facial expressions with free strokes. The model was sleepy and I have tried capturing the essence of it. Also, the use of some fluorescent shades heped me balance the values altogether.

title: Lilian, from life
desc: Lilain, from life was painted directly from observation. I was drawn to the quiet, relaxed pose and the way the warm skin tones sit against the pink bedding and dark hair. I wanted to capture the stillness of the intimate moment while responding to the colours and forms as I saw them.

title: Before we became Four
desc: This portrait explores the quiet emotional space of motherhood in transition. The sitter, seven months pregnant with her second child and already a mother to a daughter, is portrayed in a moment of reflection and anticipation. Her stillness holds the weight of identity, tenderness and change—the intimate pause before her family enters a new chapter. Through direct observation, I seek to preserve not only likeness, but the human story held within a face and gesture.

title: Ramdas
desc: “Ramdas” is one of the works from a series called “Roop- Swaroop.” This series is an attempt to understand the forms and Essence of the world around us including ourselves. At the age of 10, my parents named me Ramdas which i believe shaped a lot of my personality later on. This self portrait is an attempt to bring me closer to both [name withheld] and Ramdas ie. my current self and the 10 year old Ramdas.

title: Silent Grace
desc:
Title: Silent Grace

Medium: Oil on Canvas

Dimensions: 13" x 13"

Technique: Alla Prima (Wet-on-Wet Oil Painting)

Artist Statement & Description:

In creating "Silent Grace," I executed the work using the Alla Prima (wet-on-wet) oil painting technique, applying fresh wet layers of paint directly over underlying wet paint . This direct method allowed me to capture the immediacy, spontaneity, and raw emotional tone of a moment frozen in quiet contemplation.

The artwork features a woman draped in a vibrant crimson red saree, resting her head softly on her arms—a posture that evokes both vulnerability and deep self-embrace. The Alla Prima process enabled me to blend colors seamlessly right on the canvas, achieving soft transitions in the skin tones and realistic, fluid folds in her traditional attire.

contrasts vibrant traditional details—such as the classic golden kangan (bangles), the red bindi, and the soft alta mark on her hand—against a textured background of warm umber tones. Working wet-on-wet allowed me to maintain smooth, expressive edge control between the subject and the background, giving the painting a painterly texture and atmospheric depth. "Silent Grace" serves as a tribute to quiet dignity, cultural roots, and the calm strength found in stillness.

title: In the Lanes of the Temple
desc:
In the lanes of the temple, a small boy stood — teeka on his forehead, hand at his lips, eyes full of quiet curiosity. He wasn’t posing. He wasn’t performing. He was simply home.
This painting was born from a real moment I captured at a temple. The crumbling arch, the deep shadow of the sanctum, the worn stone steps — and in the middle of it all, this boy. Unbothered by the ancient world around him because it was never ancient to him. It was just Tuesday.
As an artist, these are the moments I live for. Not the grand or the glamorous — but the still, unguarded, deeply human ones. Oil on canvas lets me slow time down. Lets me stay in that lane a little longer. Lets me share what my eyes felt with yours.
This piece is called “In the Lanes of the Temple.”
If it made you feel something, save it, share it, or tell me in the comments. Every word of support helps an independent artist keep creating.

title: Where Are You?
desc: I painted this little girl in a moment of quiet sadness, her gaze turning away as if searching for someone beyond the frame. The soft blue dress and pale flowers surround her with innocence, while the dark background deepens the feeling of solitude. I have captured the childhood longing without explaining it.

title: The Weight of Victory
desc:
This painting depicts the “Weight of Victory” carried by a warrior after taking many lives in war as part of his duty. Although he has fulfilled his role and emerged victorious, he remains emotionally trapped by the violence and suffering he has witnessed. Warriors are often expected to be strong, fearless, and emotionless, yet beneath that exterior, they are human beings who experience the full spectrum of emotions. The painting explores this contrast between the strength expected of a warrior and the emotional burden carried by the human within.

Medium: Oil on Linen
Size: 28 in X 32 in

title: A Study in Resolve
desc:
"A Study in Resolve" is more than just a portrait; it is an attempt to capture inner strength and confidence.
​In portrait painting, basic elements like drawing, light and shadow, facial planes, tonal values, and color temperature are very important. However, while working on this piece, the subject’s sharp eyes, intense gaze, and raised eyebrows gave the painting its true meaning and life.
​Beyond technical rules, this is an honest attempt to put the character and quiet power of the subject onto paper. I used warm colors for the face and body against a simple, neutral background to make the subject stand out. This allowed me to enjoy the brushwork and the play of colors while keeping the main focus clear.
​I believe that true beauty lies in simplicity and natural realism, and that is what I tried to show in this portrait.

title: Unspoken
desc:
Acrylic on paper, size 22*23 inches.
The painting signifies a man that sits in silence fidgeting, words on the tip of his tongue, thoughts that he would like to profess but is unable to do so.

title: UNSPOKEN
desc:
A quiet conversation between pain and beauty, where the fish carry messages that words cannot express. A moment of stillness, longing, and emotions flowing beneath the surface.

Oil on linen
Size : 76 cm×89 cm

title: A quiet morning
desc: This piece is all about capturing a fleeting moment of deep thought and solitude. It shows a woman wrapped in a saree, just sitting and reflecting as a dramatic burst of warm, golden sunlight streams in from behind her.

title: The Gaze
desc:
Medium: Oil Medium
Size: A3

title: The burning horizon watcher
desc: The burning horizon watcher (2026) is life drawing study realized in 3 hours. The oil painting depicts a man facing the burning horizon seating on the ground,  astonished and crushed simultaneously by the great spectacle.

title: TASHAN
desc: "This captivating portrait of a Rajasthani shepherd masterfully captures the depth of human expression, highlighted by the intricate play of light that dances across the variations in his skin tone. Every wrinkle on his weathered face tells a story, beautifully juxtaposed against the vibrant hues of his traditional turban. To ensure the main subject commands absolute priority, the artist has rendered the background in a palette of light tones, applied with bold, deliberate brushstrokes. Executed in acrylic on canvas, this striking piece measures 24" x 36"."

title: Balya
desc: This oil Pastel painting is a portrait of my friend Balya, whom I met at a place where I was working as a freelancer. What began as a professional meeting slowly became a friendship, and I found myself noticing the quiet character behind his presence. I was drawn to his personality, his stillness, and the way his face carried a sense of experience and individuality. Instead of creating a polished or idealized portrait, I wanted to capture him as I saw him in that moment—real, unposed, and thoughtful. I painted this work directly in front of him, which made the process more personal and spontaneous. The rough marks, earthy colours, and unfinished background reflect the honesty of that encounter and our friendship.

title: Aaba
desc: This oil pastel portrait of my grandfather began with my fascination for the traces of time on him. The wrinkles on his face and the folds of his simple vest caught my attention—not as signs of age, but as marks carrying memories, experiences, and years of living. I found a quiet beauty in these details and wanted to bring them into focus through painting. The face became more than a physical likeness; it became a landscape shaped by time. I was drawn to the contrast between the warm tones of his skin, the worn texture of the fabric, and the deep surrounding darkness. Through loose marks and strong light, I tried to capture not only his appearance, but the silence, warmth, and dignity that I associate with him.

title: Svayam (a self portrait)
desc:
Svayam Tells the Story of my own Journey in Life. A self Portrait I created while Contemplating on the
ways I percieved my life. The Challenges I Persevered through while wakling the path bestowed upon
me.
Svayam is a study I did upon myself and contemplated on how my own beliefs and Conditioning were
shaping my being into existence. My Body (made of an amalgum of Wet-Paper sheets) forming and
destroying itself simoultaneuosly. each paper depicts a belief, a doubt, a self- fulfilling prophecy, a faith,
a desire in itself. Each paper is a paper from my Journnal of Life, shaping and deshaping me into
exstence. somewhere complete, and somewher incomplete.
Me in state of absolute stillness, observing this whole process and letting it flow through my being in
the form energy the build around my body while I focus on my breathing sitting on all papers holding
the walks of my past, present and future.

title: A Quiet Anticipation
desc:
Pallete used:Zorn's pallete
Description:
In the quiet glow of a dimly lit room, she waits—draped in crimson, a color that speaks of passion, longing, and unspoken dreams. Time moves slowly around her, like the soft ticking of an unseen clock. The vintage walls hold memories of countless evenings, but tonight feels different.

Her gaze drifts beyond the room, beyond the lamp’s warm light, toward a love that has not yet arrived. Perhaps it is a promise whispered by the night, or a memory of a moment yet to come. The silence around her is not empty; it is filled with anticipation.

Every fold of the red gown reflects the depth of her heart—hopeful, patient, and quietly strong. She is not merely waiting for someone; she is waiting for a feeling, a connection, a story to begin.

And in that still moment between longing and arrival, love lingers softly in the air.

title: Apathy
desc:
Title: Apathy
Medium: charcoal on paper
Size:  23×17 sq. Inches

In my drawing titled 'Apathy' I convey a sense of emotional exhaustion and numbness. Her expression is that of disinterest in the day to day activities and she feels disconnected from the people around her life.

Using charcoal as the medium I tried to bring the nuance of her internal state through the expression she bears on her lips and her half open eyes. The Moody atmosphere and the wrapping of her dress is symbolic to the turmoil that surrounds her.

title: Puratanadrishti ( पुरातनदृष्टि ) | Watercolor on paper
desc: A silent echo in a frozen stare~like an old soul waiting for a familiar share.

title: Antardrishti ( अंतर्दृष्टि ) | Watercolor
desc: The quiet power of a woman's gaze: perceiving in a fleeting second is what takes the world a lifetime to understand.

title: Rahasyagamini ( रहस्यगामिनी ) Watercolor on paper
desc: She looks like an ocean of secrets you were never meant to uncover.

title: The Maiden
desc: A study of Victorian grace, where white ruffles and pearls frame the quiet expression of a young lady.

title: Between Flesh and Form
desc: Between Flesh and Form explores the dialogue between the lived human body and the idealized permanence of classical sculpture. A seated male figure, rendered through warm earthy tones and expressive brushwork, confronts fragmented plaster forms that embody an inherited canon of beauty. The contrast between the vulnerable, aging body and the luminous sculptural ideal establishes a critical meditation on temporality, corporeality, and artistic representation. Draped blue fabric functions as both a compositional anchor and cultural signifier, while the restrained interior intensifies the psychological atmosphere. Through juxtaposition, chiaroscuro, and tactile modelling, the painting questions how art constructs, preserves, and ultimately challenges ideals of the human body.

title: Anandi Bai
desc: This is a live portrait of Anandi Bai, who worked with us for many years and became a part of our family. She would be in her 70s. In spite of her hard and tiring work, she always carried a smile on her face. This portrait was made as one of my parting gifts for her, with an attempt to capture her warmth, strength and the quiet dignity with which she lived her life.

title: Monoj
desc:
In this watercolor portrait, I have sought to capture the model’s personality and quiet expression through light, color, and spontaneous brushwork. The warm skin tones contrasted with cool blue and violet hues create depth and a sense of three-dimensionality, while the subtle interplay of light and shadow defines the facial structure.

I have intentionally kept the clothing and background loose and unfinished to preserve the freshness and immediacy of the painting, allowing the variety of brushstrokes to remain visible

title: राखणदार — The Guardian
desc:
राखणदार — The Guardian

A lone shepherd stands proudly with his flock, representing care, courage, and responsibility. His simple attire and strong presence reflect the dignity of rural life. The staff in his hand symbolizes his duty to protect, while the peaceful landscape creates a sense of silence, strength, and belonging.

“राखणदार” is a tribute to the quiet guardians who protect, nurture, and carry responsibility without seeking recognition.

title: Door to Dreams
desc:
“Door to Dreams”
It never opens often
When it does
Time will sieze
Light will gently kiss
Wind whispers
Butterflies will fly

title: The Divine Form of Kathakali – Cultural Art of Kerala
desc: This artwork is deeply inspired by the rich heritage of Kerala's world-renowned classical dance-drama, Kathakali. Set against a striking black background, the intricate portrayal features the traditional green facial expression adorned with an elaborate crown, golden ornaments, and bead embellishments, capturing the majestic grandeur of the art form. Created using a mixed media technique involving acrylic paints, beads, and dimensional detailing, this piece beautifully reflects the vibrant essence of Indian classical heritage.

title: Her Smile,1991
desc: I made this charcoal portrait of my wife in 1991 as a gift for our first wedding anniversary. A few days before our anniversary, we had gone out to a garden where I took a photograph of her. I later used that photograph as my reference for this portrait. It remains special to me because it was made from a simple personal moment and became a memory of our first year together.

title: Self Portrait
desc: I painted this self-portrait in acrylic as a study of my own face and expression. Portraits have always interested me, and I wanted to try capturing myself in colour rather than in charcoal or pencil. It was a different experience to be both the artist and the subject.

title: Bond
desc: A powerful portrait of motherhood, tradition, and the deep connection between a mother and her child.

title: JOGATI
desc:
" JOGATI "
Oil on Canvas
"जोगती"
या कलाकृतीत तृतीयपंथीय व्यक्तीचे अस्तित्व , भावविश्व श्रद्धा आणि स्वाभिमान यांचे संवेदनशील चित्रण केले आहे. देवीच्या सान्निध्यातील तिची शांत मुद्रा तिच्या अंतर्मनातील भावना आणि समाजात सन्मानाने स्वीकारले जाण्याची तिची इच्छा व्यक्त करते.

ही कलाकृती वेगळ्या ओळखी पलीकडील माणुसकी आणि भावनांचा सन्मान अधोरेखित करते.

title: REBIRTH  - A Portrait of Love, Life and New Beginnings
desc:
REBIRTH – The Beginning of a New Life

Rebirth is a heartfelt portrayal of the beautiful bond between a father and his newborn baby. The painting captures a precious moment of tenderness, love, and emotional connection as the father gently holds his newborn child.

In our lives, we experience rebirth in many ways. The birth of a baby is one of the most beautiful forms of rebirth, symbolizing a fresh beginning, renewed hope, unconditional love, and endless possibilities.

Through this painting, I want to express that when a baby is born, a new life begins not only for the child but also for the parents. It marks the beginning of a new journey filled with love, responsibility, dreams, and hope.

The peaceful expression of the father and the innocence of the newborn represent the beauty of life's most precious moments.

REBIRTH is a celebration of life, love, and the beautiful new beginnings that make our existence meaningful.

“Every birth is not just the beginning of a new life, but the rebirth of love, hope, and dreams.”

title: Self Portrait at 27
desc: This is a self portrait in oils that I did when I had short hair. After learning to draw and paint in oils I wanted to create a self portrait in the traditional manner, using all the tools and techniques I now know, painting the portrait correctly but also leaving some brushstrokes and marks unattended which I belive will later become my style. Painting portraits is a complex process of correct drawing and colour application balancing it with swiftness and a mark making which differentiates it from a photograph. I plan to make self portrait for the rest of my life to have a sort of collection to go back to.

title: Daddy
desc:
Oil on canvas.
I have always been fascinated with portraits and being from engineering background didn’t have much exposure to the basics of drawing. I have learned by observing artists on the internet like Scott Burdick . Susan Lyon , Promod Kurlekar , Prem Awale, Casey child, Jeff hein and many more.

My dad always wanted me to paint his portrait, and this felt like the perfect sign to finally do it. This piece is a tribute to a father who didn't raise me based on gender roles, but simply raised me to be a human being.Funny thing , he actually dislikes the reference photo because he was forced to wear formals for his anniversary, but it holds a special place in my heart as a dedication to him.

title: Aai
desc: This painting portrays a mother in a resting position after a long day of work. The relaxed posture is in opposite direction to light. She ignores herself and focuses on her family. That’s why the yellow garment becomes the symbol of warmth, life and the presence she has given to her family. The composition is in diagonal perspective of a body as she is focusing in different direction rather than towards the viewer. The folds are treated through variations of warm and cool tones, allowing the fabric to create both volume and movement; in contrast with warm light and cool shadow. The painting has a quiet emotional presence found within an everyday moment.

title: Dripping joy
desc:
Joy doesn't need a reason.
Dripping Joy celebrates happiness in small moments — a soapy, fleeting, unposed laugh captured in charcoal, where foam pops and joy overflows.

title: Childhood in Bloom
desc: In this painting I want to express the innocence, happiness, beauty and the carefree joy of childhood. I tried to capture a cheerful young girl enjoying a bright peaceful day outdoor. She is dressed in a lovely white and lavender frock. Her short dark hair frames her smiling face, expressing innocence, happiness and youthful energy. The soft sunlight illuminates her face and dress creating a warm and lively atmosphere. Behind her the shades of blue, green and yellow blend together to suggest a beautiful natural setting. The girl's relaxed pose and joyful expression make the scene feel natural and heartwarming. Overall through this art I want to beautifully celebrate childhood, innocence, freedom and the simple happiness found in nature.
